props.title: Jaws

sections.content: Jaws revolutionized blockbuster filmmaking through Steven Spielberg's masterful tension-building and John Williams' iconic two-note theme. The film's genius lies in withholding the shark for most of the runtime, forcing viewers to imagine the terror lurking beneath. This technique, born partly from mechanical shark malfunctions, created a template for monster movies like Alien (1979) and The Thing (1982). The dynamic between Roy Scheider's cautious Chief Brody, Richard Dreyfuss's scientific Hooper, and Robert Shaw's hardened Quint delivers character depth rarely seen in thriller films.

sections.content: The success of Jaws spawned numerous marine horror films, though few matched its psychological complexity. Deep Blue Sea (1999) amped up the action with multiple intelligent sharks, while The Reef (2010) returned to minimalist survival horror. 47 Meters Down (2017) trapped its protagonists in a shark cage, proving the subgenre's enduring appeal. But Spielberg's original triumph wasn't just about shark attacks - it explored small-town politics, masculinity, and human responses to invisible threats.

The film's influence extends beyond horror. Close Encounters of the Third Kind (1977) and Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981) followed Spielberg's pattern of gradual revelation and character-driven suspense. The beach attack scene, with its innovative dolly zoom on Brody, became a masterclass in conveying psychological shock, later echoed in countless thrillers like Vertigo (1958) and Goodfellas (1990). movies.title: The Abyss
movies.slug: James Cameron's deep-sea alien encounter thriller

sections.content: While modern shark films rely heavily on CGI, Jaws proved the power of practical effects and suggestion. The mechanical shark's limitations forced creative solutions that heightened suspense. This approach influenced later practical effects masterpieces like The Thing (1982) and Jurassic Park (1993), where tangible threats created visceral audience responses. Even modern films like The Shallows (2016) combine practical and digital effects to recapture that physical menace.
